_schema.applies_to: matcher on {components, scenarios, periods, results}; null = any. components: Table 4.2 money columns (static_cost, intensive_margin, extensive_margin, net_fiscal_cost); scenarios: central, high_cost, low_cost; periods: claim periods (the tax year's later year); results: certified (the certified-pair run) or published_dashboard (the history row)
_schema.status: the comparison status this annotation sets, where it sets one; at most one status-setting annotation matches a result
_schema.basis: traceability: raw/pages_layout.txt (PDF page and printed page), engine files at the certified pin, or the measured artifact results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json

annotations.text: Both numbers are static costs. CenTax's static cost is the cost of funding the hours for children of parents above £100,000 before any behavioural response (Table 4.2 notes; Appendix A, 'Static cost'). PolicyEngine's is the change in spending on the three free-hours entitlements with the limit removed and no behavioural response run.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 42 (printed page 41, Table 4.2 notes) and PDF pages 75-76 (printed pages 74-75, Appendix A 'Static cost'); results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json behavioural_response 'none (static)'; policyengine_uk 2.89.2 applies labour-supply responses only through Simulation.apply_dynamics (simulation.py), which pipeline/compute_uk_childcare_100k.py never calls

annotations.text: A static cost on both sides, but the published PolicyEngine figure is the engine plus the dashboard's six local corrections to policyengine-uk 2.102.3, so it is a construction rather than the engine as served.

CenTax's net fiscal cost adds two behavioural gains to the static cost: tax from parents who stop holding their income below £100,000 (the intensive margin) and tax and National Insurance from partners who enter work (the extensive margin). PolicyEngine's counterpart is the static cost alone, so the two measure different things.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 42 (printed page 41, Table 4.2 notes: 'The intensive margin behavioural gain ... The extensive margin behavioural gain ...') and PDF page 76 (printed page 75, Appendix A 'Behavioural revenue gain')

annotations.text: CenTax's scenarios assume different falls in the bunching friction after 2022 (none in the high-cost scenario, a 50% fall in the low-cost one). That changes how many parents are above £100,000 under current law, so the static cost differs by scenario. PolicyEngine has one current-law income distribution, so one PolicyEngine value meets all three scenarios.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF pages 40-41 (printed pages 39-40, section 4.1) and PDF page 75 (printed page 74, Appendix A 'Static cost': parents between £100,000 and the marginal buncher's income)

annotations.text: CenTax costs the free childcare hours only ('removing the £100,000 threshold for eligibility for free childcare hours'). Tax-Free Childcare, which has its own £100,000 limit, is not part of the reform. PolicyEngine's counterpart matches: it removes only the 30-hours limit and sums the three free-hours entitlements, and the run measured no change in Tax-Free Childcare. The £500 Tax-Free Childcare addition in CenTax's Appendix D belongs to the Centre for British Progress estimate CenTax reviews, not to CenTax's figures.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 42 (printed page 41, Table 4.2 notes), PDF page 9 (printed page 8, section 1.1: Tax-Free Childcare 'withdrawn in full ... once either parent has an ANI above £100,000') and PDF page 100 (printed page 99, Appendix D: CBP's 'value of the entitlement ... with £500 added for Tax-Free Childcare'); results/uk/childcare_100k/<variant>.json worlds.free_hours: limits_executed and the tax_free_childcare sum

annotations.text: CenTax names tax years by their later year, so 2028 is 2027-28 and 2030 is 2029-30. PolicyEngine's annual period 2027 runs the 2027-28 rules: policyengine-uk sets each government parameter for year Y to its value on 30 April of Y.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 3 (printed page 2, editorial note: 'tax year 2021-22 is given as 2022'); policyengine_uk 2.89.2 utils/parameters.py convert_to_fiscal_year_parameters, called in tax_benefit_system.py process_parameters

annotations.text: CenTax costs the free childcare hours only. The dashboard's reform also removed the Tax-Free Childcare limit; the figure here is its 30-hours leg, which excludes Tax-Free Childcare (the dashboard puts that leg at £0.159bn in 2027-28 and £0.173bn in 2029-30).
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 42 (printed page 41, Table 4.2 notes); pe/published_dashboard.json (budget.gross_bn.thirty_hours and budget.gross_bn.tax_free_childcare of data/results.json at f25f0db)

annotations.text: CenTax names tax years by their later year, so 2028 is 2027-28 and 2030 is 2029-30. The dashboard names fiscal years by their start year (2027 is 2027-28) and compared its 2029-30 figure with CenTax's 2030.
annotations.basis: raw/pages_layout.txt PDF page 3 (printed page 2, editorial note); pe/published_dashboard.json (src/childcare_100k/config.py at f25f0db: 'Fiscal years named by start year ("2026" = 2026-27)'; data/results.json benchmarks[0].like_for_like)
